items.followUp: Differentiate between a web browser and a web server.

rubric.why: A server provides services or resources to other computers on a network.
rubric.description: Describes the role of a server system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a server provides services or resources.

rubric.why: A client requests services or resources from a server and uses them.
rubric.description: Describes the role of a client system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a client requests services or resources from a server.

modelAnswer: A server system provides services or resources to other computers on a network.
A client system requests and uses the services or resources provided by a server.

items.followUp: Differentiate between software testing and debugging, giving an example of each.

rubric.why: Verification checks that the product is being developed according to its specified requirements.
rubric.description: Defines verification by relating it to specified requirements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating what verification checks.

rubric.why: Validation checks whether the completed product meets users’ needs or intended use.
rubric.description: Defines validation by relating it to users’ needs or intended use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating what validation checks.

rubric.why: Reviewing a design or code against requirements is an example of verification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example of verification.

rubric.why: Having users test completed software against their needs is an example of validation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example of validation.

modelAnswer: Verification checks whether the product is being developed according to specified requirements; it asks, “Are we building the product right?”
Example: reviewing a design or code to check that it follows the requirements.
Validation checks whether the completed product meets users’ needs; it asks, “Are we building the right product?”
Example: users test the completed software to see whether it performs the tasks they need.

items.followUp: Explain four advantages of using a computer network.

rubric.why: Networks allow connected users to share hardware devices rather than requiring separate devices for each computer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a network lets users share hardware, such as printers.

rubric.why: Networks allow users to share files, data and software.
rubric.description: Explains sharing files, data or software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing information or software sharing.

rubric.why: Networks support communication between users, including through email and video conferencing.
rubric.description: Explains communication as a reason for using a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing communication enabled by a network.

rubric.why: Resource sharing and central management can reduce costs and simplify administration.
rubric.description: Explains reduced costs or easier administration through central management.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly explained additional benefit.

modelAnswer: A computer network allows users to share hardware, such as printers, instead of needing a separate device for each computer.
Users can share files, data and software over the network.
A network enables fast communication between users through services such as email or video conferencing.
Sharing resources and managing data centrally can reduce costs and make administration easier.

items.followUp: Explain any four ways people can protect themselves from cyber crime.

rubric.why: Hacking involves gaining unauthorised access to computer systems or data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming hacking and describing unauthorised access to a system or data.

rubric.why: Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to trick people into revealing sensitive information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming phishing and explaining how it tricks people into revealing information.

rubric.why: Identity theft uses another person’s personal information to impersonate them or commit fraud.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming identity theft and describing fraudulent use of another person’s identity or information.

rubric.why: Software piracy is the illegal copying or distribution of copyrighted software.
rubric.description: Names and explains another cyber crime, such as software piracy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming software piracy and describing illegal copying or distribution of software.

modelAnswer: Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to a computer system or its data.
Phishing is using fake emails or websites to trick people into revealing passwords or other personal information.
Identity theft is using another person’s personal information to impersonate them or commit fraud.
Software piracy is illegally copying or distributing copyrighted software.

items.followUp: Explain the steps in the top-down design approach to solving a problem.

rubric.why: Divide and Conquer begins by breaking a large problem into smaller, manageable subproblems.
rubric.description: Describes dividing the problem into smaller parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the division step.

rubric.why: The smaller problems are solved and their results combined to solve the original problem.
rubric.description: Describes solving the subproblems and combining their results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing both the solving and combining steps.

modelAnswer: Divide a large problem into smaller, manageable subproblems.
Solve the subproblems and combine their results to produce the solution to the original problem.
